ruleset.name: opik-backend-code-style
ruleset.description: Opik backend code style: inline fully-qualified name gate.

rule.name: InlineFullyQualifiedName
rule.message: Inline fully-qualified name ''{0}'': import the type at the top of the file and use its simple name. If a simple-name collision in this file makes the FQN unavoidable, append '// NOPMD - <reason>' to the line.
rule.description:
Types from any external package — java.*, jakarta.*, io.dropwizard.*, lombok.*, reactor.*, third-party — must be imported at the top of the file and referenced by their simple name, not written out fully qualified inline. This is a general heuristic, not a per-namespace allowlist: the convention is "import at the top", and it does not depend on which library the type comes from.
Two exclusions, both structural rather than stylistic:
1. com.comet.opik.* self-references are out of scope for OPIK-7832. Same smell, but excluded to keep this change's blast radius to external types.
2. Nested-type access (Alert.View.Public, Schema.AccessMode.READ_ONLY) is NOT an inline FQN — it is how you reference a nested type, and often cannot be shortened at all. PMD reports the nested path in @PackageQualifier as a flat string, identical in shape to a package, and without full type resolution (which a fast pre-commit hook does not have) the AST offers no attribute that tells the two apart. The discriminator below is therefore the Java naming convention: a package qualifier's FIRST segment is lowercase (java.util, io.dropwizard.core, vendor.API), while a nested-type path begins with a class name and is therefore uppercase (Alert.View). Only the first segment is constrained, so an uppercase segment later in a real package (vendor.API.Type) is still caught. Without this the rule fires ~300 times on the codebase's standard @JsonView pattern.
A fully-qualified name is legitimate when two types share a simple name in one file (java.util.Date vs java.sql.Date, java.util.stream.Stream vs a domain Stream) — an import can only cover one of them — or in any other case where the inline form is deliberate. Suppress those with a trailing '// NOPMD - <reason>' on the offending line, or @SuppressWarnings("PMD.InlineFullyQualifiedName") on the declaration. The reason is the point: it is what makes the exception reviewable.
